To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the detection of a pure tone masked by broadband amplitude‐modulated masking noise in the presence of a slow and coherent modulation of the noise can be explained by a suppression of neuronal response locking to the modulation by low‐level pure tones.
the detection of tones in noise is facilitated by the presence of amplitude modulations in the noise, and that this is due to the suppression of the amplitude modulation locking in auditory cortex.

the auditory cortex can detect a pure tone in the presence of broadband noise when the noise is amplitude modulated, and the detection is based on the suppression of amplitude‐modulated responses to the noise by low level tones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the auditory system extracts information from complex acoustic signals.
the mechanisms of sound detection in the presence of fluctuating noise.
the detection of tones masked by noise in the auditory cortex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the detection of tones in modulated broadband noise is mediated by a combination of the suppression of locking to the amplitude modulation in the presence of the tones and of the detection of energy in the frequency band of the tones.

detection thresholds for pure tones masked by modulated noise were lower than those masked by unmodulated noise due to the suppression of the neuronal locking of the neuronal response to the amplitude modulation in modulated noise.

the detection of low‐level tones masked by fluctuating noise is based on a combination of two factors: (i) the reduction in the masking noise level due to the modulation of the masking noise, and (ii) the suppression of the neuronal locking to the modulation of noise by low‐amplitude tones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the detection of low‐level tones in noise is facilitated by the presence of amplitude modulation in the noise.

detection of tones in amplitude‐modulation noise is based on a combination of suppression of amplitude modulation and the ability of the auditory system to extract pure tone information in the presence of a fluctuating masker.
the detection of a pure tone masked by broadband noise depends on the ability of the neuronal responses in auditory cortex to suppress the modulation of the masker.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection threshold of a low‐level tone in noise can be reduced by exploiting the temporal structure of the noise.
, even when the signal‐noise ratio is very small, the auditory system can use information about the statistics of the background to detect a signal.
the auditory system can exploit the temporal structure of the masker in order to detect a tone embedded in the masker.
